subject: Tyke Hikes, leaf sunprints and Santa at CityCentre
preheader: Plus: a new lawn-and-playhouse hangout is coming to Memorial City.
intro: It's a quiet stretch in Spring Branch, but there are a few good ones. Sunday, Nov 15 is Tyke Hikes en español at the Arboretum for your 18-months-to-4 crowd, and on Thursday, Nov 19 the Spring Branch Memorial library has a free leaf sunprint craft for older kids and tweens.

Thanksgiving week is a school break (Nov 23–27), so pencil in Saturday, Nov 28 for Santa and reindeer in the CityCentre plaza, and Friday, Dec 4 for the free Frozen movie night in Memorial Park. One heads-up: the library's homeschool workshop and tween book club are already full, so skip those unless you're on the list.

items.title: Greenside, a family-friendly spot with a kids' play structure, is coming to Memorial City
items.description: A new family-friendly hangout built around a one-acre lawn is coming to 1085 Gessner, with a children's play area in the plans. Michelin-recognized Pizzana is among the restaurants opening there this fall.
paragraphs: A new family-friendly hangout built around a one-acre lawn is coming to 1085 Gessner, with a children's play area in the plans. Michelin-recognized Pizzana is among the restaurants opening there this fall.

image.alt: Illustration: A naturalist leads toddlers and preschoolers with parents along a shady woodland trail, kids pointing at leaves and a pond, strollers on the path

items.title: Tyke Hikes en español
items.description: A Spanish-language nature walk for ages 18 months to 4 with a grown-up: a story, a sensory activity and a stroller-friendly hike. Younger siblings welcome. Parking is $6.50.

image.alt: Illustration: Kids outside a library holding colorful fall leaves over blue light-sensitive paper in the afternoon sun, a librarian showing them how to press the leaves flat

items.title: Fall Leaf Sunprints
items.description: A STEM craft for kids and tweens: pick fall leaves outside and use light-sensitive paper to make blue cyanotype sunprints.

items.title: Tyke Hike at Arrowwood Pond
items.when: Select Mondays: Nov 2, 9, 16, then Dec 7, 14, 21 · 9:30 am–10:15 am
items.description: A naturalist leads a story, a simple nature activity and a stroller-friendly trail hike for ages 18 months to 4 with a grown-up. Two sessions, 9:30 and 10:30 am.

items.title: Stories & Crafts in the Cabin
items.description: A nature story and craft in the sanctuary's log cabin for ages 3–5 with an adult. Siblings with a supervising adult come free.

items.title: Hatchlings outdoor play for babies
items.cost: $12 members / $15 nonmembers per child and caregiver
items.description: **Registration is full** for 2026 classes; check for a waitlist. Messy outdoor play with sand, mud, sticks and leaves for ages 0–18 months with a caregiver. Bring a change of clothes.

items.title: Baby Bouncers playtime
items.description: Bouncy songs, rhymes and playtime for crawlers and babies taking their first steps. Two sessions, 10:15 and 11:15.

items.title: Toddler storytime
items.description: Books, songs and movement for ages 18–36 months with a caregiver.

items.title: Tiny Tykes storytime
items.description: Interactive storytime for new walkers and their grown-ups: stories, songs and finger plays. Two sessions, 10:15 and 11:15. Some weeks it's outside in the Reading Garden.

items.title: Feges BBQ
items.description: Kids eat free on Wednesdays, 5 pm–8 pm. Barbecue with a big patio and a small enclosed play space with a climbing gym tucked beside it. You order at the counter, so no waiting in line with wiggly kids.

items.title: Yard House
items.when: CityCentre · $$ · Kids' menu, Lawn to run
items.description: Big menu, kids' menu, and it sits right on CityCentre's plaza lawn, where kids can run around before or after dinner.

items.title: Blue Agave Cantina
items.description: Tex-Mex near Terry Hershey Park with a patio playground. Pair it with an afternoon on the trails.

image.alt: Illustration: A warm, realistic, candid photo in a Houston family kitchen on a sunny November afternoon, landscape

items.title: Forced "thank yous" aren't gratitude. Here's what works at 2, 4 and 6.
items.description: Your toddler won't say thank you on cue? That's not ungrateful, it's development. What thankfulness really looks like in little kids, plus Thanksgiving traditions that work.

image.alt: Illustration: A warm, realistic, candid photo on a cozy living room couch on a gray November morning in a Houston home, landscape

items.title: Runny nose, no fever? Your kid can probably go to daycare.
items.description: Green snot, a cough, a fever at 6 am: what pediatricians and Texas child care rules actually say about keeping little ones home, and when it's fine to send them in.

items.title: SBISD Thanksgiving break
items.description: No school all week. Plan library visits and park days early, since popular spots fill up.

items.title: Holiday in the Plaza
items.description: Meet Santa and two of his reindeer, with free professional photos, plus holiday singing and dancing. A donation for the SPCA is welcome. Santa leaves at 4 pm, so arrive on time; weather permitting.

items.title: Neighborhood Nights: Holiday Edition
items.description: A free holiday evening on the lawn: Frozen movie at 6 pm, photos with Santa, Anna and Elsa, letters to Santa, a train ride, cocoa and food trucks. Bring a blanket; no strollers or bikes. Listing end time varies (8 or 9 pm).

items.title: SBISD winter break
items.description: Two weeks off school. We'll round up winter break camps and indoor ideas in December.
